name: Singapore
tagline: Two street stalls, two Michelin stars, and full meals for under 3 dollars.

Hawker Chan.description: The world's cheapest Michelin-starred soy sauce chicken rice, since 2016. The first Asian street stall to achieve it.

Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice.description: Singapore's most popular Hainanese chicken rice stall, inside the Maxwell Food Centre. Michelin star, and a must-stop for Anthony Bourdain on 'No Reservations'.

Odette.description: Modern French cuisine from chef Julien Royer inside the National Gallery. Three Michelin stars since 2019.

Newton Food Centre.description: One of Singapore's first hawker centres, since 1971, with more than 80 open-air Chinese, Malay, and Indian stalls.

Lau Pa Sat.description: A Victorian national monument turned food market, famous for its "Satay Street" at nightfall.

Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle.description: A bak chor mee (minced pork noodle) stall with a Michelin star since 2016; chef Tang Chay Seng closes as soon as the day's ingredients run out, creating multi-hour queues.

Jumbo Seafood.description: The flagship chain of Singapore's chili crab since 1987, with its original outlet at the seaside East Coast Seafood Centre; one of the addresses most cited by international critics for the national dish.

Long Beach Seafood Restaurant.description: Founded in 1946 and credited with inventing black pepper crab; its Dempsey Hill location remains a classic address for Singaporean-style seafood.

Ya Kun Kaya Toast.description: A kaya toast chain founded in 1944 by Loi Ah Koon; its original China Street outlet still serves the classic breakfast of kaya toast, butter, and soft-boiled eggs.

Toast Box.description: A modern-'kopitiam'-style kaya toast chain founded in 2005 that recreates the look of Singapore's traditional Chinese coffee shops with toast, kopi, and eggs.

328 Katong Laksa.description: One of Katong's most famous laksa stalls, traditionally served with only a spoon (the noodles are cut into short lengths) in a heavily spiced coconut broth.

Sungei Road Laksa.description: A laksa stall running since the 1950s, known for selling only a limited number of portions each day and keeping the same spicy coconut broth recipe for more than seven decades.

Zam Zam Restaurant.description: Founded in 1908 on North Bridge Road across from the Sultan Mosque; specializing in murtabak and biryani, it is one of Singapore's oldest Indian-Muslim restaurants.

Tekka Centre.description: A market and hawker centre in the heart of Little India, with Indian, Malay, and Chinese food stalls alongside a traditional wet market.

Chinatown Complex Food Centre.description: Singapore's largest hawker centre, with close to 200 stalls; home to several vendors recognized with the Michelin Guide's Bib Gourmand.

Amoy Street Food Centre.description: A hawker centre in the Tanjong Pagar financial district, packed at lunchtime with office workers drawn to its traditional Chinese food stalls.

Burnt Ends.description: A contemporary wood-fire grill restaurant by Australian chef Dave Pynt; one Michelin star and a regular on the Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list.

Candlenut.description: The world's first Peranakan restaurant to earn a Michelin star, led by chef Malcolm Lee at Dempsey Hill.

Labyrinth.description: A contemporary reinterpretation of hawker and traditional Singaporean dishes by chef LG Han; one Michelin star, located in Esplanade Mall.

Les Amis.description: Singapore's longest-running French restaurant still in operation, holding three Michelin stars and one of Asia's most awarded wine lists.

Waku Ghin.description: A fine-dining Japanese restaurant by chef Tetsuya Wakuda at Marina Bay Sands, serving a limited-seat tasting menu built on daily flown-in ingredients.

Meta.description: Contemporary Asian cuisine from chef Sun Kim on Keong Saik Road; one Michelin star.

Violet Oon Singapore.description: A restaurant by renowned chef Violet Oon inside the National Gallery, devoted to classic Peranakan dishes such as ayam buah keluak and kueh pie tee.

True Blue Cuisine.description: A family-run Peranakan restaurant across from the Peranakan Museum, serving recipes passed down through generations of the Nyonya community.

Din Tai Fung.description: A Taiwanese chain famous for its xiao long bao; its 2002 opening at Paragon was Din Tai Fung's first location outside Taiwan and Japan.

Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao.description: A local chain founded in 1991 specializing in hand-made xiao long bao and la mian noodles; one of Singapore's most established Chinese restaurant brands.

CE LA VI.description: A rooftop bar and restaurant atop the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark, with panoramic bay views and signature cocktails.

Long Bar.description: The historic bar at Raffles Hotel where bartender Ngiam Tong Boon invented the Singapore Sling cocktail in 1915; famous for its floor of discarded peanut shells.

Atlas Bar.description: An Art Deco bar in Parkview Square holding one of the world's largest gin collections (over a thousand labels) and a three-story champagne tower.

Manhattan Bar.description: A classic American cocktail bar at The Regent Singapore hotel, named Asia's best bar multiple times on the Asia's 50 Best Bars list.

Jigger & Pony.description: A cocktail bar at the Amara Hotel led by Bannie Kang, named Asia's best bar in 2018 on the Asia's 50 Best Bars list.

Tiong Bahru Bakery.description: A bakery founded by French chef Gontran Cherrier in the Tiong Bahru neighborhood, celebrated for its kouign-amann.

Song Fa Bak Kut Teh.description: A bak kut teh (pork rib pepper soup) specialist since 1969, recognized with the Michelin Guide's Bib Gourmand at its original New Bridge Road outlet.

Founder Bak Kut Teh.description: One of the oldest bak kut teh restaurants on Balestier Road, running since 1978, serving a clearer, more peppery broth than the Hokkien style.

No Signboard Seafood.description: Born as a nameless stall (hence 'No Signboard') in Geylang in the 1970s; now a chain known for its white pepper crab.

Killiney Kopitiam.description: A family-run kopitiam on Killiney Road operating since 1919, serving kaya toast, kopi, and laksa in a shop that has barely changed its look.

Maxwell Food Centre.description: A hawker centre in the heart of Chinatown that Anthony Bourdain toured on 'No Reservations'; home to dozens of stalls, including Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice.

Old Airport Road Food Centre.description: A hawker centre highly rated by locals for the quality of its stalls, including hokkien mee and satay bee hoon specialists with decades of history.

Sin Huat Eating House.description: An unassuming Geylang eatery famous for its crab bee hoon (crab noodles); Anthony Bourdain visited it in the Singapore episode of 'No Reservations'.

Chin Chin Eating House.description: A kopitiam-restaurant on Purvis Street since 1934, specializing in Hainanese chicken rice and chicken curry; one of Singapore's oldest eateries.
